title: DEEPSUB: a free submarine horror game where sonar gives away your position (AI-assisted, seeking playtest feedback)
author: Notausgang09
selftext:
I've put an early build of DEEPSUB on [itch.io](http://itch.io) and would love some outside playtesting.



You pilot a sealed submarine using sonar, still photographs and a hydrophone. The catch is that the engine and sonar make noise, and something in the water hunts by sound. You have to choose between getting more information and giving away your position, while keeping the air, battery and hull intact. There are story dives, a seeded free-dive mode, and a safe SEA TRIALS training dive to learn the instruments.



On the AI side, this is a Godot/GDScript project with AI-assisted code and mission dialogue. The creature mesh and much of the ambience are generated in code, alongside CC0 Kenney assets. Verification uses headless tests, scripted dive runs and cockpit screenshots. That checks whether the systems work, but it leaves the part that needs real players: whether the cockpit is understandable and the tension feels fair.



Free Windows 10/11 (64-bit) build: [https://levisager11-oss.itch.io/deepsub](https://levisager11-oss.itch.io/deepsub)

Actual gameplay screenshots: [https://deepsub-images.vercel.app/](https://deepsub-images.vercel.app/)



Start with SEA TRIALS. I'd especially like to know where you first felt confused, whether the instrument text is readable, and whether using sonar versus staying quiet feels like an interesting choice. If you hit a bug or get stuck, the last thing you tried would really help. Even feedback from a short session would be useful.



It's an early build, so handling, creature behaviour and audio still need human playtesting. Headphones recommended. The Windows executable is unsigned, so SmartScreen may show a warning. Thanks for taking a look!
